standard_prerequisites.name: The partition number p(G) and the cover number c(G)
standard_prerequisites.statement: p(G) is the minimum m such that the edge set of G is the union of m edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs of G, and c(G) is the same number without the edge-disjointness requirement, so that c(G) is at most p(G); retained at source lines 128-129, with comparability graphs described at source lines 117-120.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts c(G) <= p(G) <= 2 for almost all perfect graphs, so both parameters and their relation must be fixed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The density classes PE(n), P2PE(n), BE(n) and GSP(n) and the meaning of almost all
standard_prerequisites.statement: PE(n) is the set of labelled perfect graphs on n vertices and P2PE(n) the subset that can be partitioned into at most two comparability graphs, so that the statement of the counted theorem is the limit of the ratios |P2PE(n)|/|PE(n)| equal to one; BE(n) and GSP(n) are the corresponding sets of labelled Berge graphs and labelled GSP graphs; retained at source lines 193-197 and 214-216.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact quantitative form of the two almost-all statements that the proof multiplies, and the identification PE(n)=BE(n) by the strong perfect graph theorem that the proof invokes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generalized split graphs and the theorem of Promel and Steger
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graph is a GSP graph when either it or its complement splits into a complete graph and a union of vertex-disjoint complete graphs with no edges between them, and almost all Berge graphs are GSP, meaning the limit of |GSP(n)|/|BE(n)| equals one; retained at source lines 204-206 and 212-216.
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the class whose partition number the proof needs to bound and the density statement that transfers that bound to all Berge graphs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every GSP graph has partition number at most two
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any GSP graph G the edge set can be partitioned into two comparability graphs of G; retained at source lines 225-226.
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts membership in GSP(n) into membership in P2PE(n), which is the inclusion the proof uses for the first limit.

core_obligations: Record the two inclusions used by the proof: GSP(n) is contained in P2PE(n), because every GSP graph has its edge set partitioned into two comparability graphs, and BE(n)=PE(n), because a graph is perfect exactly when it is Berge, by the strong perfect graph theorem (source line 246-247).
Write the resulting chain of limits: the ratio |GSP(n)|/|BE(n)| is at most |P2PE(n)|/|PE(n)|, which is at most one (source line 249).
Use the theorem of Promel and Steger, which gives that the first limit equals one (source lines 247-251).

Conclude by the squeeze principle that the limit of |P2PE(n)|/|PE(n)| also equals one, which is the statement that almost all perfect graphs can be partitioned into two comparability graphs (source line 250).

proof_roadmap.step: Take the inclusion of the GSP graphs among the partitionable perfect graphs and identify the Berge graphs with the perfect graphs.
Write the sandwich of the three density limits that the two inclusions give.
Apply the Promel-Steger limit for the outer term and the squeeze principle to conclude.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem twocover（源 190-191 行，证明 246-250 行）：证明「几乎所有完美图都满足 c(G)<=p(G)<=2」。证明的关键不是例行核验：必须先把两个密度类之间的包含关系摆对——GSP(n) ⊆ P2PE(n) 来自本线的 Theorem gensplit，而 BE(n)=PE(n) 来自强完美图定理（246-247 行），于是三个极限形成夹逼 |GSP(n)|/|BE(n)| <= |P2PE(n)|/|PE(n)| <= 1（249 行），再由 Pröm el-Steger 定理给出外层极限为 1，才能推出中间极限为 1（250 行）。难点在于两个包含的方向与分母的选择必须与「almost all」在两种类上的精确定义一致，任何一处取反都得不到结论；原文位置在证明的 246-249 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Theorem twocover at source lines 190-191 together with the author's proof, whose header at source line 246 names the theorem as Proof of Theorem twocover; the proof is not adjacent to the statement, because the article places the discussion of almost all, the definition of GSP graphs, the theorem of Promel and Steger and the theorem on GSP graphs in between, so the pairing rests on the author's own named header rather than on a later-first-proof rule.

The retained context at source lines 117-120 and 128-129 is the article's own description of comparability graphs and its definitions of p(G) and c(G); the retained context at source lines 193-197, 204-206, 212-213 and 214-216 is its own explanation of the term almost all, its definition of GSP graphs and its statement of the theorem of Promel and Steger with its limiting meaning.

The retained context at source lines 225-226 is the article's own theorem that every GSP graph has partition number at most two, which the proof uses as the inclusion of GSP(n) in P2PE(n). It is retained as a prerequisite; its own proof is not part of this material.

The retained context at source lines 212-213 carries the author's citation to the paper of Promel and Steger, and the bibliography fragment attached to this task carries that single entry copied verbatim from the author's own bibliography at source line 750; no entry was rewritten, added or reordered.

The source preamble cannot be retained as it stands: it loads rawfonts, psfrag, verbatim, tikz with several libraries, hyperref with the pagebackref option and a dvi driver option for graphicx, none of which the retained body spans use, and it redefines backref commands that only exist because of that hyperref option. The retained preamble file therefore carries, line for line, source line 2, source line 3, source line 4, source line 16, source line 17, the theorem declarations of source lines 20-30 and the author macro definitions of source lines 32-41; the only textual change anywhere is the removal of the dvipdfm driver option from the graphicx line, because the assembly forces the xelatex engine. No new macro, package or declaration was introduced.

The article's Theorem promelsteger and Theorem gensplit are cited here only through their statements in the retained context, their proofs are not retained, and the article's other results, namely Theorem bipline, Theorem unit, Theorem co-triangulated, Theorem loglog, Theorem ub, Lemma rec, the corollaries genupbound, shift, doblesh and p', and Proposition H9, are not counted here.
